programme.title: Jesse Stone: Stone Cold
programme.desc: Der Mord an einem jungen Mann erschüttert die Kleinstadt Paradise. Zwei saubere Einschusslöcher in der Brust lassen auf das Kaliber der Waffe schließen, doch sonst finden sich weder Spuren noch Verdächtige. Als auf einem Parkplatz eine weitere Leiche mit zwei Kugeln in der Brust gefunden wird, zeichnet sich ein Muster ab. Polizeichef Jesse Stone steht vor einem Rätsel, denn zwischen den Opfern gibt es keine Verbindung - aber wer in der kleinen Stadt tötet aus purer Mordlust.

programme.title: Sea Patrol
programme.desc: S1 E7 — Mayday!Die Crew der Hammersley erhält immer wieder mysteriöse Notrufe von einer jungen, äußerst attraktiven Seglerin, die für einen guten Zweck alleine um die Welt segelt. Sie gibt an, immer wieder von Piraten attackiert zu werden. Während die Männer an Bord dem Charme der hübschen Frau schnell erliegen, haben Nikki und Kate Zweifel an den widersprüchlichen Aussagen der Seglerin.

programme.title: Sea Patrol
programme.desc: S1 E8 — BombenstimmungNach einem heftigen Zyklon werden zwei zwölfjährige Jungen auf Hoher See vermisst. Anscheinend waren die beiden allen Warnungen zum Trotz heimlich rausgefahren. Nachdem die beiden Jungen gefunden wurden, zeigen sie Spider ihre geheime Hütte, in der die Kinder allerlei Fundstücke und Treibgut sammeln. Darunter auch eine Seemine aus dem 2. Weltkrieg, deren Sprengung beinahe eines der Kinder tötet.

programme.title: Yellowstone
programme.desc: S2 E5 — Den Feind berührenJamie versucht vor lauter Verzweiflung alles, um einen Fehler wiedergutzumachen. Jimmy ist unterdessen damit beschäftigt, sich etwas Geld dazuzuverdienen. Kayce stellt Dan bezüglich der toten Rinder auf der Ranch zur Rede.

programme.title: S.W.A.T.
programme.desc: S2 E12 — Einsatz in MexikoJessica und Chris gehen auf eine gefährliche Undercover-Mission in Mexiko. Hondo beschäftigt sich unterdessen mit Renovierungsarbeiten.

programme.title: S.W.A.T.
programme.desc: S2 E13 — Der zweite AktDie S.W.A.T.-Cops bekommen es erneut mit der Bande zu tun, die ihnen vor drei Monaten entkam. Diesmal entführen die Gangster Mitarbeiter von Konzernen, die sie als korrupt betrachten und fordern ein Lösegeld in Millionenhöhe.

programme.title: S.W.A.T.
programme.desc: S2 E14 — Das B-TeamHondo trifft eine alte Flamme wieder, die als Special Agent beim FBI arbeitet. Bei einem Charity-Wettbewerb versucht das S.W.A.T.-Team alles, um die Feuerwehr von Los Angeles auszustechen.

programme.title: Red Eye
programme.desc: S1 E2 — Folge 2Während Nolan um sein Leben fürchtet, steigen die Spannungen an Bord. Hana wird vom Leiter des britischen Geheimdienstes MI5 beauftragt, Nachforschungen anzustellen. Hanas Schwester beginnt, den Ereignissen der NCA 357 nachzugehen.

Cedar Cove - Das Gesetz des Herzens
programme.desc: S1 E4 — WiedergutmachungenEric nimmt Jack voll in Anspruch. Er manipuliert ihn und nutzt seine Schuldgefühle schamlos aus. Darunter leidet die Beziehung zwischen Jack und Olivia, bis Grace Jack den Kopf zurechtrückt. Maryellen bietet Justine einen Stand auf dem jährlichen Kunstmarkt an. Die kann ihr Glück kaum fassen und baut ihn mit Seths Hilfe schnell auf. Sich der Öffentlichkeit zu stellen, ist hart für Justine, aber sie meistert die Aufgabe souverän.

programme.title: Cedar Cove - Das Gesetz des Herzens
programme.desc: S1 E5 — Der Kinder wegenOlivia hat in einem komplizierten Scheidungsverfahren zu richten. Beide Parteien kommen nicht über ihre Verletzungen hinweg und geraten immer wieder in einen selbstzerstörerischen Streit. Es gelingt Olivia nicht, Mr. und Mrs. Westen zum Wohle der Kinder zu einer einvernehmlichen Einigung zu führen. Am Ende gewährt sie die Scheidung.

programme.title: Cedar Cove - Das Gesetz des Herzens
programme.desc: S1 E6 — Sieg über die AngstMaryellen erfährt, dass John aus der Not heraus Fotos verkaufen möchte: Er hat seinen Job als Koch verloren. Maryellen hilft ihm, in Cedar Cove Arbeit zu finden, und möchte ihm am liebsten auch noch eine Wohnung besorgen. John scheint mit ihrem Verhalten überfordert zu sein. Auf einen Rat ihrer Mutter hin hält sich Maryellen etwas zurück und landet damit bei John den ersten Erfolg.

programme.title: Cedar Cove - Das Gesetz des Herzens
programme.desc: S1 E7 — VorurteileJack und Olivia fahren nach Seattle. Aber aus dem romantischen Abenteuer wird nichts, denn das Spiel der Mariners dauert so lange, dass Olivia eingeschlafen ist, bevor Jack zurückkommen konnte. Allison kann den Dauerstreit ihrer geschiedenen Eltern Rosie und Zach nicht mehr ertragen. Sie möchte bei Peggy und Bob einziehen, aber die haben schon Rosie ein Zimmer vermietet. Nun muss Allison auch hier noch die Klagen ihrer Mutter anhören.

programme.title: Cedar Cove - Das Gesetz des Herzens
programme.desc: S1 E8 — Wer bietet mehr?Stan bittet Olivia, ihn zur Psychotherapie zu begleiten, wo sie sich mit ihren emotionalen Verletzungen aus der Zeit nach Jordans Tod konfrontiert sieht. Zum ersten Mal fangen die beiden an, darüber zu reden, und machen die ersten Schritte hin zum Verzeihen. Stan war jedoch zu feige, seiner Frau Melanie von der Therapiestunde mit Olivia zu erzählen. Melanie ist wütend und Stan verdrückt sich, so wie früher.

programme.title: Flower Shop Mystery: Mum's the Word
programme.desc: Die New Yorker Anwältin Abby Knight kehrt in ihre Heimat, eine kleine Stadt, zurück. Sie hat vor, dort einen Blumenladen aufzumachen. Am Tag der Eröffnung beobachtet Abby jedoch einen Täter dabei, wie er gerade vom Tatort flieht. Abby steht vor einer Menge unbeantworteter Fragen und beschließt, nach Antworten zu suchen. Gemeinsam mit einem charmanten Barkeeper beginnt sie die Ermittlungen in dem Fall.

programme.title: The Invisible Woman
programme.desc: Die junge Schauspielerin Nelly Ternan erregt bei einem ihrer Auftritte im Londoner Haymarket Theatre die Aufmerksamkeit des Schriftstellers Charles Dickens. Der verheiratete Vater besetzt die 17-Jährige in der Theaterproduktion "The Frozen Deep" und die beiden beginnen schließlich eine leidenschaftliche Affäre. Bis zu ihrem Lebensende erfährt die Öffentlichkeit nichts von ihrer Liebe, denn die gesellschaftlichen Konventionen verlangen es so. Und so führt Nelly ein Leben im Schatten.

programme.title: Mr. Miracle
programme.desc: Harry Mills ist ein Engel und wird für seine erste weihnachtliche Mission auf die Erde geschickt. Er soll der Studentin Addie Folsom bis Heiligabend dabei helfen, den Tod ihres Vaters zu verarbeiten, und ihr Leben wieder in den Griff zu bekommen. Diese Aufgabe erweist sich als schwieriger als gedacht, denn Harry lernt, dass Menschen anders sind, als er vermutet hatte. Somit lernt er viel über die Verhaltensweisen der Menschen.

programme.title: Flower Shop Mystery: Snipped in the Bud
programme.desc: Abby Knight besitzt einen Blumenladen. Während einer Lieferung an ihre alte Universität begegnet sie ihrem langjährigen Rivalen aus dem Jurastudium. Dieser wird kurz darauf tot aufgefunden. Abby gerät schon bald unter Mordverdacht und die Beweislage scheint immer erdrückender für sie zu werden. Abby beschließt, die Ermittlungen selbst in die Hand zu nehmen. Dabei macht sie erstaunliche Entdeckungen.

programme.title: Little Women (2019)
programme.desc: Jo, Meg, Amy und Beth sind Schwestern und wachsen Mitte des 19. Jahrhunderts in den Vereinigten Staaten auf. Zu dieser Zeit herrschen starre Geschlechterrollen. Ihr Vater dient im Bürgerkrieg und ihre Mutter kümmert sich um die Familie und arbeitet. Die Schwestern wachsen heran und stellen fest, dass viele Hindernisse als Frauen auf sie warten. Jo will Schriftstellerin werden und sich dem Rollendiktat nicht unterwerfen, während Meg von der Ehe und Amy vom Malen in Paris träumt.

programme.title: Atlantic Crossing
programme.desc: S1 E1 — Die FluchtDie Kronprinzessin Märtha und der Kronprinz Olav von Norwegen befürchten eine deutsche Invasion in ihrem Land. Aber das Kabinett glaubt nicht an eine ernsthafte Bedrohung und erkennt die Gefahr erst, als es schon viel zu spät ist.

programme.title: Atlantic Crossing
programme.desc: S1 E2 — Der ThronWährend Olav weiterhin in London ausharren muss, lebt Märtha vorübergehend im Weißen Haus. Dort erobert der Präsident die Herzen der Kinder im Sturm, doch Ragni warnt Märtha, nicht auch seinem präsidentiellen Charme zu erliegen.

programme.title: Atlantic Crossing
programme.desc: S1 E3 — EntfremdungDie Reise von Kronprinzessin Märtha über den Atlantik wird dramatisch. In den Vereinigten Staaten angekommen, wird sie eingeladen, ins Weiße Haus einzuziehen, wo Präsident Roosevelt sie und den kleinen Harald mit Aufmerksamkeit überhäuft.

programme.title: Atlantic Crossing
programme.desc: Als die von Roosevelt angekündigte Militärhilfe, die er Norwegen zugesagt hat, nicht erfolgt, wählt Märtha den Weg in die Öffentlichkeit, um das amerikanische Volk um Hilfe zu bitten. Doch gerade als sie erste Erfolge erzielt, trifft sie ein unerwarteter Rückschlag. Offensichtlich für jedermann, erweisen sich die Gefühle des Präsidenten ihr gegenüber als tiefer, als es die Freundschaft erlaubt.

programme.title: Atlantic Crossing
programme.desc: S1 E5 — VerbündeteDie versprochene Munition aus den USA nach Norwegen fehlt. Märtha veranstaltet eine Dinnerparty, um die Unterstützung der Kongressabgeordneten für ein Gesetz zu gewinnen. Der Präsident scheint eine Grenze mit Märtha zu übertreten.

programme.title: Atlantic Crossing
programme.desc: S1 E6 — WendepunktMärtha verspricht Olav, den Präsidenten nicht wiederzusehen, doch dann kommt es zu einer Bedrohung.

programme.title: Atlantic Crossing
programme.desc: S1 E7 — Das GeschenkOlav beschuldigt Märtha, die Kinder in große Gefahr zu bringen und stellt ihr ein klares Ultimatum. Außerdem wird Märtha in Verlegenheit gebracht, als Präsident Roosevelt ankündigt, dass er ihr und Norwegen ein bedeutendes Geschenk machen wird.

programme.title: Atlantic Crossing
programme.desc: S1 E8 — Eine Königin kehrt zurückMärtha erleidet einen großen Verlust und muss sich entscheiden, ob sie in den USA bleibt oder gemeinsam mit den Kindern nach Norwegen zurückkehrt. Doch bevor sie ein neues Leben beginnen kann, gibt es eine letzte Schlacht, der sie sich stellen muss.

programme.title: Candice Renoir
programme.desc: S4 E7 — Die ganze Wahrheit verschweigt man besserNach der gemeinsamen Nacht kehren Antoine und Candice aus Valenciennes zurück. Vor Ort erfahren sie, dass Sylvie Leclerc den Posten von Attia übernommen hat. Die Leiche einer jungen Frau führt die Ermittler zu gefälschten Alibis und Geheimnissen.

programme.title: Candice Renoir
programme.desc: S4 E8 — Kein Rauch ohne FeuerIn einem Internetforum taucht die anonyme Meldung auf, dass in Sète ein Kind entführt wurde. Dazu gibt es ein Foto von Entführer und Opfer. Die Nachricht verbreitet sich rasant in den Medien. Eine Falschinformation behindert zunächst das Team.

programme.title: Candice Renoir
programme.desc: S4 E9 — Seine wahren Freunde erkennt man erst im UnglückAntoine gesteht Candice, dass er Jennifer verlassen will. Es kommt zu Spannungen im Team. Die Leiche eines Mannes wird gefunden, der laut seiner Frau illegal Taxi gefahren ist. Doch dann entdeckt das Team eine Verbindung zu einem Fall von 1979.

programme.title: Candice Renoir
programme.desc: S4 E10 — Auge um Auge und die Welt erblindetDer Psychiater Dr. Adler warnt die Polizei, dass eine Patientin aus der Klinik abgehauen sei, um Antoine zu ermorden. Der nimmt die Warnung nicht ernst, doch dann explodiert eine Bombe. Der Sprengstoffanschlag wurde vor dem Präsidiumsgebäude verübt.

programme.title: Candice Renoir
programme.desc: S5 E1 — Gebeichtet ist halb vergebenAls im Rahmen eines Firmenseminars eine Teilnehmerin tot aufgefunden wird, entdecken Candice und ihr Team schnell, dass die in der Gesellschaft gut angesehene Frau so sehr in Lügengespinste verstrickt war, dass sie nicht mehr herauskam.

programme.title: Murdoch Mysteries - Auf den Spuren mysteriöser Mordfälle
programme.desc: S10 E10 — Teufel im KopfEin Mann wurde verhaftet, weil er zwei Bewohnern die Kehlen durchgeschnitten hat. Der Mörder, Jacob Foley, behauptet, vom Geist von James Gillies besessen zu sein, der ihn angeblich zu den beiden Verbrechen getrieben habe.

programme.title: Murdoch Mysteries - Auf den Spuren mysteriöser Mordfälle
programme.desc: S10 E11 — Murdoch auf vier PfotenMurdoch untersucht den Tod eines Showhunds und bemerkt eine verborgene Zuneigung zu Hundebegleitern.

programme.title: Murdoch Mysteries - Auf den Spuren mysteriöser Mordfälle
programme.desc: S10 E12 — Der verlorene EnkelsohnZwanzig Jahre nach der Entführung eines Kindes untersucht Murdoch die Identität eines Mannes.

programme.title: Murdoch Mysteries - Auf den Spuren mysteriöser Mordfälle
programme.desc: S10 E13 — Tödliche NachbarschaftAls Murdoch und Ogden ihr Grundstück am Flussufer als Begräbnisstätte nutzen, um die Zersetzung von Leichen zu untersuchen, graben sie mehr aus, als sie sich vorgestellt hatten.

programme.title: Murdoch Mysteries - Auf den Spuren mysteriöser Mordfälle
programme.desc: S10 E14 — Ewige JugendMurdoch entwickelt ein Elixier, das jugendliche Vitalität zurückbringt. Crabtree beunruhigt das.

programme.title: Murdoch Mysteries - Auf den Spuren mysteriöser Mordfälle
programme.desc: S10 E15 — Im Reich der GöttinnenEine Explosion, in die eine geheimnisvolle Frau verwickelt ist, der Watts nachgeht, führt Murdoch zu einer geheimen Gemeinschaft.

programme.title: Murdoch Mysteries - Auf den Spuren mysteriöser Mordfälle
programme.desc: S10 E16 — Mr. LovecraftDie Entdeckung der Leiche eines jungen Mädchens, sowie einiger grotesker Zeichnungen, führt Murdoch zu dem Verdacht, dass eine Gruppe von Jugendlichen, die vom Tod besessen sind, dahintersteckt. Unter ihnen ist auch ein gewisser H. P. Lovecraft.

programme.title: Murdoch Mysteries - Auf den Spuren mysteriöser Mordfälle
programme.desc: S10 E17 — Das RollschuhrennenDer Tod einer professionellen Rollschuhläuferin wirkt zunächst wie ein Unfall. Bei seinen Ermittlungen stößt Murdoch auf Rivalitäten im Wettkampf und er findet sich alsbald in einer Welt von gnadenlos ehrgeizigen jungen Frauen wieder.

programme.title: Murdoch Mysteries - Auf den Spuren mysteriöser Mordfälle
programme.desc: S10 E18 — In die Enge getriebenNach politischen Intrigen wird Murdoch des Mordes verdächtigt und gerät selbst ins Visier der Polizei. Während seine Kollegen an seine Unschuld glauben, bleibt wenig Zeit, eine gefährliche Verschwörung aufzudecken.

programme.title: Murdoch Mysteries - Auf den Spuren mysteriöser Mordfälle
programme.desc: S1 E1 — PowerDer katholische Detektiv William Murdoch hat es nicht leicht im Toronto des 19. Jahrhunderts, denn die Stadt ist mehrheitlich protestantisch geprägt. Zudem stoßen seine Aufklärungsmethoden auf die Skepsis seines Vorgesetzten.

Die Zeremonie verläuft ohne weitere Vorfälle, sodass Abby endlich erleichtert aufatmen kann. Doch plötzlich entdecken sie und der ehemalige Privatdetektiv Marco die Leiche von Jack Sutcliff. Der eigentlich fröhliche Tag nimmt eine rätselhafte Wendung.

programme.desc: S2 E1 — Gefährliche GefühleInspektorin Petra Delicato muss ihren Urlaub für eine Mordermittlung vorzeitig beenden. Am Tatort gibt es für sie eine Überraschung: Der Tote ist ihr durchaus bekannt. Es handelt sich um einen Anwalt, mit dem sie am Tag zuvor ein Sexdate hatte.

programme.title: The Silent Storm
programme.desc: In Schottland bemüht sich der protestantische Minister Balor McNeil um den Zusammenhalt seiner Gemeinde. Seine nicht vom Eiland stammende Ehefrau Aislin befindet sich mehr mit der Natur im Einklang als mit den anderen Bewohnern des Dorfes. Die Ehe der beiden gestaltet sich schwierig, vor allem Balors Zorn und Gewalt prägen den Alltag des Paares. Als die McNeils den jungen Straftäter Fionn zur Resozialisierung bei sich aufnehmen, gerät ihre Welt Stück für Stück aus den Fugen.

programme.title: Candice Renoir
programme.desc: S5 E2 — Zwei WeltenDie Spuren an einem Tatort sind durch Löscharbeiten fast alle vernichtet. Dennoch ist schnell klar, dass es sich nicht um einen Unfall handelt. Das männliche Opfer wurde durch einen Kopfschuss getötet und dann mit dem Wohnwagen in Brand gesetzt.

programme.title: Cedar Cove - Das Gesetz des Herzens
programme.desc: S1 E9 — Alte Flamme, neuer FunkeStan ist froh mit Olivia zum Starkwater Lake gegangen zu sein. Jack, der Olivia nicht erreichen konnte, ist zu ihr gefahren und beobachtet das vertraute Beisammensein der beiden. Er ist verunsichert, ob es zwischen ihnen noch Gefühle gibt. Olivia überrascht Jack mit Karten für ein besonderes Baseballspiel. Seth schlägt Justine vor, zu ihm aufs Boot zu ziehen, aber sie bringt ihn stattdessen dazu, dass er bei ihr einzieht, was Olivia mit Sorge sieht.

programme.title: Grand Hotel
programme.desc: S1 — Die goldene MesserspitzeEine Prostituierte wird ermordet aufgefunden und die in der tödlichen Wunde gefundene goldene Klinge weist zum Grand Hotel. Währenddessen verdichten sich Hinweise und machen Alicias Verlobten Diego zum Hauptverdächtigen.

programme.title: Candice Renoir
programme.desc: S5 E2 — Zwei WeltenDie Spuren an einem Tatort sind durch Löscharbeiten fast alle vernichtet. Dennoch ist schnell klar, dass es sich nicht um einen Unfall handelt. Das männliche Opfer wurde durch einen Kopfschuss getötet und dann mit dem Wohnwagen in Brand gesetzt.

programme.title: Murdoch Mysteries - Auf den Spuren mysteriöser Mordfälle
programme.desc: S1 E2 — The Glass CeilingEin Richter und ein Anwalt werden ermordet. Murdoch versucht, einen Zusammenhang zwischen den Männern herzustellen, und stellt fest, dass beide mit der Verurteilung eines Kleinkriminellen zu tun hatten. Der Fall stellt die Ermittler vor ein Rätsel.

programme.title: Murdoch Mysteries - Auf den Spuren mysteriöser Mordfälle
programme.desc: S1 E3 — AusgeknocktDer professionelle Boxer Amos Robinson sollte eigentlich einen Kampf absichtlich verlieren, doch im Ring schlägt er seinen Gegner k. o. Als Robinson noch am selben Abend ermordet wird, befasst sich Murdoch mit dem kuriosen Fall.

programme.title: Grand Hotel
programme.desc: S1 — Die goldene MesserspitzeEine Prostituierte wird ermordet aufgefunden und die in der tödlichen Wunde gefundene goldene Klinge weist zum Grand Hotel. Währenddessen verdichten sich Hinweise und machen Alicias Verlobten Diego zum Hauptverdächtigen.

programme.title: Candice Renoir
programme.desc: S5 E2 — Zwei WeltenDie Spuren an einem Tatort sind durch Löscharbeiten fast alle vernichtet. Dennoch ist schnell klar, dass es sich nicht um einen Unfall handelt. Das männliche Opfer wurde durch einen Kopfschuss getötet und dann mit dem Wohnwagen in Brand gesetzt.

programme.title: Cedar Cove - Das Gesetz des Herzens
programme.desc: S1 E9 — Alte Flamme, neuer FunkeStan ist froh mit Olivia zum Starkwater Lake gegangen zu sein. Jack, der Olivia nicht erreichen konnte, ist zu ihr gefahren und beobachtet das vertraute Beisammensein der beiden. Er ist verunsichert, ob es zwischen ihnen noch Gefühle gibt. Olivia überrascht Jack mit Karten für ein besonderes Baseballspiel. Seth schlägt Justine vor, zu ihm aufs Boot zu ziehen, aber sie bringt ihn stattdessen dazu, dass er bei ihr einzieht, was Olivia mit Sorge sieht.

programme.title: Sanditon
programme.desc: S3 E2 — Folge 2Charlotte bleibt in Sanditon, um Georgiana bei ihrem Kampf um ihr Erbe zu beizustehen. Leo hofft indes, dass sie und Colbourne wieder zusammenkommen werden. Sir Edward bittet Augusta um Hilfe beim Verfassen eines Gedichts.

programme.title: Murdoch Mysteries - Auf den Spuren mysteriöser Mordfälle
programme.desc: S10 E18 — In die Enge getriebenNach politischen Intrigen wird Murdoch des Mordes verdächtigt und gerät selbst ins Visier der Polizei. Während seine Kollegen an seine Unschuld glauben, bleibt wenig Zeit, eine gefährliche Verschwörung aufzudecken.

programme.title: Murdoch Mysteries - Auf den Spuren mysteriöser Mordfälle
programme.desc: S8 E5 — Folge 14Während ihrer Flitterwochen in New York decken Murdoch und Ogden eine Verschwörung auf, die das Leben von Präsident Teddy Roosevelt gefährdet. Brackenreid und Doktor Grace untersuchen einen bizarren Autounfall in Toronto.

programme.title: Houdini & Doyle
programme.desc: S1 E3 — In Manus Dei?Übersinnliches oder Mord - das müssen Houdini, Doyle und Adelaide klären, als ein Mann tot zusammenbricht, nachdem er bei der Vorstellung eines Gesundbeters laut dessen Talent als Heiler angezweifelt hatte. Für Doyle ist der Fall besonders wichtig.

programme.title: Houdini & Doyle
programme.desc: S1 E4 — Ein furchtbares Phantom?In London stirbt ein Geschäftsmann. Er ist umgebracht worden von einem Phantom mit teuflischen Augen, das fliegen kann. Als weitere Attentate folgen, muss das Team untersuchen, was hinter der sich ausbreitenden Massenhysterie wirklich steckt.

programme.title: Archie - Die Cary Grant Story
programme.desc: S1 E1 — Folge 1Cary Grant ist in Los Angeles und macht seine dritte Scheidung durch. Wir blicken auf seine schwierige Kindheit als Archie Leach in Bristol zurück, mit einem tyrannischen Vater und einer Mutter, die um seinen Bruder trauert. Nachdem Archies Vater ihm sagt, dass seine Mutter tot ist, folgen wir dem Teenager Archie nach New York, auf der Suche nach Ruhm und Reichtum. In der Zwischenzeit sieht der 58-jährige Cary die schöne 26-jährige Dyan Cannon in einer Fernsehshow und beginnt, sie zu umwerben.

Full Circle with Michael Palin
programme.desc: An ambitious adventure of discovery awaits intrepid TV comedian-turned-global explorer Michael Palin, as he journeys around the Pacific rim to meet disparate communities which share a common coastline. This is his third great trek, having circumnavigated the world and traversed from North to South Poles in earlier series. Palin's personable character shines through as he makes new friends and learns about the culture and lifestyles of peoples who inhabit islands, archipelagos, shorelines and ocean-facing nations across the hemispheres. Setting out from Alaska, the ex-Python star visits Japan, Korea, China, Vietnam, the Philippines, Australia, New Zealand, Chile, Bolivia, Peru, Columbia, Mexico, the USA and Canada, before returning to his departure point. Get ready for a close-up view of volcanoes, rainforests and coral reefs, and a privileged insight into regional cuisines, cultural ceremonies and cities buzzing with entertainments and bristling with off-the-tourist route attractions. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Natural World
programme.desc: Wildlife documentary featuring the fascinating lives of Britain's beautiful butterflies filmed in exquisite detail, and also a celebration of their enduring appeal to the British people. Butterfly-costumed carnival-goers dance at Notting Hill, street artist Nick Walker uses their image to brighten bare city walls, burlesque dancer Vicky Butterfly recreates butterfly dances, and women reveal their butterfly tattoos at Britain's biggest tattoo convention. Britain's butterflies have never been so threatened, three-quarters are in decline – but do they still have a message for us? A search for butterflies leads to some of the most beautiful parts of Britain. It opens up the intriguing possibility that a passion for butterflies could help us preserve the landscapes that we love. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: A Stitch in Time
programme.desc: Documentary series that combines biography, art and the history of fashion as host Amber Butchart, a fashion historian, explores the lives of historical figures – Marie Antoinette, Charles II, Dido Belle, Edward the Black and others, by examining the clothes that they wore. Amber looks into the history of the garments and the people depicted, visiting collections and speaking with experts. Alongside Amber, historical tailor Ninya Mikhaila and her team recreate key garments using the original techniques. The viewers have a chance to see Amber wear the recreated clothing at the end of each episode. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: BBC Young Musician
programme.desc: The famous competition was established by Humphrey Burton, Walter Todds and Roy Tippin in 1978, and invites talented British musicians under the age of 18 years old to showcase their abilities. Performers of keyboard, percussion, brass, string and woodwind can enter the iconic classical competition, with five stages for them to advance through; regional auditions, category auditions, category finals, semi-finals and the final. Previous winners include pianist Lauren Zhang in 2018 for her Prokofiev Concerto no.2, violinist Nicola Benedetti CBE in 2004 and composer and clarinetist Mark Simpson in 2006. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Shakespeare: Rise of a Genius
programme.desc: A 30-year-old Shakespeare is at the top of his game: he's got a job at England's best theatre company, the Lord Chamberlain's Men, and the money is rolling in. Determined to restore his family's reputation, Shakespeare works harder than ever, producing hit after hit: A Midsummer Night's Dream, Henry IV and Julius Caesar. But as his star rises, a series of tragedies strike. Shakespeare's life, purpose and family is thrown into chaos, and he begins to question if his new life is worth the sacrifice. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Remembers...
programme.sub-title: Derek Jacobi Remembers... Much Ado About Nothing
programme.desc: Sir Derek Jacobi looks back on the filmed version of Franco Zeffirelli's famous 1960s production of Much Ado About Nothing – a performance that brought together Robert Stephens, in the role of Benedick, and his soon-to-be wife – the late, great Maggie Smith – in the key role of Beatrice. For years, this recording was considered to be 'lost' by Shakespeare fans and TV historians, until a copy was found in the US in 2010 and then restored. Here, Derek recalls how working under 'Zeff' with such an impressive cast made for one of his personal career highlights, helped in no small part by the presence of Dame Maggie onstage and the friendship they enjoyed behind the curtain. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: New Zealand: Earth's Mythical Islands
programme.desc: New Zealand was one of the last land-masses to be found and settled by people. Lush and fertile, almost everything brought here flourishes, often with surprising consequences. Told through the experiences of its native species – in particular, a charismatic and peculiar giant, flightless parrot – this is the moving story of the changing fortunes of New Zealand's wildlife, since humans first arrived. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: The Latest Secrets of Hieroglyphs
programme.desc: The great history of Egypt is inscribed on its monuments, temples and tombs, but hieroglyphs – the written language of the ancient Egyptians – fell silent until 1822 when a young French scholar, Jean-François Champollion, became the first person to decipher their texts for over a thousand years. Champollion's insights and the work of other scholars helped bring an entire civilisation back to life. Today, researchers are increasingly interested in the authors who created these hieroglyphic works. Near Luxor, The Latest Secrets of Hieroglyphs follows a new generation of Egyptologists as they unlock the texts inscribed inside a richly adorned tomb, revealing the beliefs and lives of the priests, scribes, painters, engravers and builders who created this grand funerary monument. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Ancient Worlds
programme.desc: In the last of the series, archaeologist and historian Richard Miles examines the rise and fall of the Roman Empire. At the height of its power, the Roman Empire extended the benefits of its civilization to a 60 million citizens and subjects in a swathe of territory that extended from Hadrian's Wall to the banks of the Euphrates. Even under the rule of mad, bad and dangerous emperors, the imperial system proved to be robust, buttressed by the support of elite families in the far-flung corners of the empire whose loyalty was ensured by a system of cultural aspiration, economic opportunity and military coercion. But the material benefits of the "good order" delivered by Roman rule provided its citizens and subjects with the security to ask profound questions about the meaning of life, questions that the pragmatic, polytheistic Roman belief system was ill-equipped to answer. Christianity grew to fill the spiritual vacuum at the heart of Roman civilization, eventually claiming an Emperor, Constantine, as its greatest prize. The City of Man would be eclipsed the City of God. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: New Zealand: Earth's Mythical Islands
programme.desc: The magical islands of New Zealand are explored in this fascinating documentary series, highlighting the country's rugged landscapes and dazzling species. Narrated by Kiwi actor Sam Neill (Jurassic Park), the series also examines New Zealand's natural history; a country that has been isolated in the South Pacific since the Jurassic period, with predators from that era still roaming its forests to this day. The islands are home to a wide variety of both native and foreign species, with the majority of them thriving in the country's diverse and lush ecosystems, and this three-part series celebrates many different species' resilience, including humans. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: Money For Nothing is a British TV program hosted by Sarah Moore, Jay Blades and EJ Osborne. The hosts save things from being dumped and transform them into valuable pieces, making money for people who had no idea there was cash to be made from their old useless stuff. Any profit is then returned to those people. The team salvage items from recycling centers and transform them into unique treasures. They manage to recycle old bowling balls, cooperate with designers to give a second life to old furniture, create a gorgeous dress from a salvaged leather sofa and work all kinds of miracles. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Bargain Hunt: on Your Marks, Get Set, GO!
programme.sub-title: On Your Marks, Get Set, Go!
programme.desc: As the Paris 2024 Olympics get under way, Bargain Hunt is getting in on the sporting action! In a special show, two teams of well-known Olympians and Paralympians battle for golden gavel glory. Natasha Raskin Sharp referees Sally Gunnell OBE and Mark Foster on the red team and Dame Sarah Storey and Richard Whitehead MBE on the blue team. Coached by Danny Sebastian and Kate Bliss, these Team GB legends dash around a huge antiques fair in Nottinghamshire to find items that meet their sporting challenges. Sally focuses on an old camera but doesn't snap it up, while Mark plans to get ahead with a giant Buddha! Meanwhile, Kate spots a four-leaf clover pendant, but there is nothing lucky about the price tag. However, there is an extra prize on offer in this special show: the chance to compete for the coveted Bargain Hunt Games Cup. Over three extraordinary events, the athletes put their skills to the test. Then it's onto the home straight when auctioneer Richard Winterton champions their items to a packed room of bidders. Who will cross the finish line with the most money? And will anyone add a golden gavel to their trophy cabinet? (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Points of View
programme.desc: Long-running British series that allows members of the public to voice their opinions on BBC television shows from recent weeks. Broadcast in a short, 10-minute-long format, each episode reads out letters/emails from viewers who wish to praise, criticise or comment on a programme that has appeared on any of the BBC's numerous channels. The series first aired back in 1961, and has continued to act as a reference point for people to have their say on the shows they've seen, whether good or bad. It has employed the services of several notable presenters over past decades, with Tina Daheley acting as narrator since 2018. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Songs of Praise: The Music Is Black
programme.desc: An exploration of religious music in Britain. The presenters look into different genres and visit churches and cathedrals around the country, where the congregations sing various classical and modern hymns and worship songs. Join to gain a better understanding of the importance of singing in Christianity. The series also includes segments like news and interviews that are of interest to the Christian viewers. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Film: The Witches (2020)
programme.desc:
Alabama, 1968. Bei einem Verkehrsunfall verliert ein siebenjähriger Junge (Jahzir Bruno) seine Eltern und kommt zur liebevollen Großmutter (Octavia Spencer) aufs Land. Es dauert nicht lange, da werden die beiden durch furchterregende Hexen um deren Großmeisterin (Anne Hathaway) bedroht. 

Sie fliehen in ein mondänes ­Hotel an der Küste – doch genau dort versammeln sich die Hexen, die alle Kinder in Mäuse verwandeln wollen. Ihre ersten Opfer sind der kleine Junge und sein neuer Freund. Können sie gemeinsam mit der Großmutter den Kampf aufnehmen?

Robert Zemeckis („Forrest Gump“) hat die Geschichte von Roald Dahl aus dem Jahr 1963 neu verfilmt. Das Abenteuer hat einen langsamen Start, ist aber gut ausgestattet, angereichert mit Black Music aus den 1960ern und Spezialeffekten, die nicht atemberaubend, für ein junges Publikum aber in Ordnung sind. 

Den Darstellenden – allen voran die herrlich diabolischen Anne Hathaway und Stanley Tucci (als Hotel­manager) – sieht man an, dass sie Spaß hatten. Doch der endet ohne Vorwarnung und Auflösung, sodass der Zuschauende ratlos zurückbleibt.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Learn the tricks of the trade when you go to the auctions with Homes Under the Hammer. Join presenters Martin Roberts, Dion Dublin and Martel Maxwell as they follow the renovation stories of properties across Britain as they get transformed from empty shells and outdated buildings to desirable spaces and contemporary homes. Watch as ordinary people breathe new life into the otherwise unloved houses, and find out how well they managed to stay within budget. Will they sell and make a profit, or have they invested too much money in a project that wont sell? (Senderinfo).

programme.sub-title: Countryfile Ramble for Children in Need
programme.desc: Discover more about the British countryside as the presenters visit rural homes and areas to bring stories about nature and wildlife and environmental topics to a wider audience. The programme focuses on seasonal subjects with an overarching theme of conservation, species protection, the preservation of the rural way of life and challenges facing modern farming communities. The Sunday morning show has been presented by John Craven since its launch, and features competitions, interviews, studio debates and market reports. Special productions include bird species census counts, with members of the public taking part in surveys, and tips for farmers, conservationists, ramblers and nature lovers alike. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Antiques valuation programme. A team of well-respected experts travel around the UK visiting a string of beautiful locations such as castles, stately homes, mansions, gardens and museums. They are met by members of the public who have brought along an antique, family heirloom or curio, eager for a current valuation. The experts have their own specialisms and are always on the lookout for a surprise discovery among the artwork, furniture, jewellery, silver, books, clothing and more. The entertainment comes from the conversations about the histories of the more interesting items, and the suspense as the owners and onlookers who gather around the stands await the experts' estimations about how much each would go for at auction. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Crimewatch Caught
programme.desc: From the team behind Crimewatch, this brand new series tells the most dramatic and heartbreaking stories of how detectives have solved their most complex cases. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Learn the tricks of the trade when you go to the auctions with Homes Under the Hammer. Join presenters Martin Roberts, Dion Dublin and Martel Maxwell as they follow the renovation stories of properties across Britain as they get transformed from empty shells and outdated buildings to desirable spaces and contemporary homes. Watch as ordinary people breathe new life into the otherwise unloved houses, and find out how well they managed to stay within budget. Will they sell and make a profit, or have they invested too much money in a project that wont sell? (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Two teams of amateur collectors meet at an antiques fair to compete to turn in the largest profit from a £300 budget. The teams receive guidance from expert traders, who give feedback on which items are most likely to attract the highest bids. The contestants first head to the High Street to acquire items they want to trade. Any leftover money is taken by their mentors, who go shopping for extra items as 'bonus buys'. The teams must decide which 'package' of goodies should be taken to auction, on the understanding that they may turn in a profit or loss on their investment decisions. The show has been on air since March 2000, being voted Most Popular Daytime Programme in 2002 and Best Lifestyle Show in 2003. It was also nominated for Most Popular Factual Entertainment Programme in 2003. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: Early afternoon round-up of the day's biggest national and international stories. The BBC News Team bring you the headlines and essential up-to-the-minute information about the latest developments. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: Jacqui Joseph is at Altrincham recycling centre in Greater Manchester with an eagle eye, hoping to swoop in on quality items before they're lost forever. She rescues an old, rusty pulley, a nursing chair and a table with cast-iron legs. With the help of robot maker Mark Haig and upholsterer Sharon O'Connor, the tired trio of items has the chance to shine once more, but will Jacqui manage to send all three upcycled items off to new homes? (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Push factors from the noisy, bustling cities of Britain, combined with the alluring peace of the countryside, has the population dreaming of homes in more scenic surroundings. Escape to the Country sees buyers from different areas on the UK considering their options to settle down in the English countryside. Presenters show off a range of prospective homes, before they must make their final decision towards the end of the show. Each episode taking place in a different region of the UK, we see a wide variety of beautiful homes across the country. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Interesting docu-reality show, hosted by English actor and presenter Nigel Havers, in which a panel of dealers provide expert advice and buy off various antique and collectable items brought in by members of the public. Nigel welcomes people who have intriguing, often peculiar and extraordinary items they want to sell- anything from toys and furniture to musical instruments, and introduces them to an expert who provides them with some information about the object. Sellers then go to the ''Bidding room'' where they meet five dealers who have to bid against each other if they want to take home these incredible items. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Join our host Ross Kemp in this suspenseful quiz, where contestants have to tread lightly in order to avoid "lies" on their way to the goal and the cash prize. The quiz tests the contestants' knowledge, but also how good they are in strategy and careful planning: stepping on the truths earns them money, while stepping on a lie means they lose half of their money, and if they step on three lies – they lose everything. Finding the right way has never been easy, but with a bit of luck they might not go back home empty-handed. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: The high pressure game show, where pointless answers are the way to win. Contestants not only have to answer questions correctly, but give the answer that scores the least points. They do this by coming up with the least obvious answers, that other people struggle to come up with in a survey of individuals. A correct answer that nobody else managed to say is a pointless answer, the best possible outcome. A pointless answer in the final round is how you win the jackpot, cash prize, which grows with every episode until someone wins. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: The One Show
programme.desc: A show with big-name guests and special reports on a range of subjects including consumer rights, current affairs and contemporary issues. The One Show looks at topics from the quirky and rare to much more serious matters. Since first hitting British screens in 2006, The One Show has welcomed hundreds of celebrities to its sofa. With high-profile from stage, screen, sport, music, politics and more; including then-British-Prime Minister Theresa May, Daniel Radcliffe, Dame Judy Dench, Sir Tom Jones and many, many more. With fun, laughs and the occasional musical number. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: EastEnders
programme.desc: EastEnders is a series set in Albert Square in the East End of London in the fictional Borough of Walford. Here respectable townhouses are next to offices and apartments. We follow everyday stories of local residents and their families. The locals live their ordinary lives- go to night clubs, markets, pubs and cafes. They fall in love and fight, get sick, get divorced. Kids can break a window, neighbors can pick a fight. There is nothing extraordinary but life in the East End is full of various moments of fun. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Have I Got News for You
programme.desc: Re-runs featuring favourite moments from the irreverent current affairs quiz show that shines a spotlight on the key news stories and scandals of the particular week in question. Satirical magazine editor Ian Hislop and deadpan comedian Paul Merton are the regular team captains who send up politicians, celebrities, royalty and sports stars and each other with due aplomb. The panel game was hosted by Angus Deayton throughout the 1990s, until he found himself embroiled in the kind of tabloid scandal that the show was designed to highlight and lampoon. The vacant chair has since been taken by a host of VIP ringmasters, from Boris Johnson to Ruby Wax, Jeremy Clarkson to Jo Brand, leading the panelists through regular topics covering TV and newspaper stories, obscure links between famous people, and the cheeky missing words from headlines round in which the teams nudge the boundaries of taste and legality. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Film: Bodies Bodies Bodies
programme.desc:
Während ein Hurrikan naht, fährt die soeben aus dem Entzug zurückgekehrte Sophie mit ihrer neuen Freundin Bee zu ihrem besten Kumpel David. Der schmeißt im elterlichen Ferienanwesen eine Party mit seiner Clique und dem älteren Greg, einer flüchtigen Tinder-Bekanntschaft. 

Die Zeit vertreibt sich die Gruppe mit „Bodies Bodies Bodies“, einem Spiel, bei dem einer die Rolle eines Killers übernimmt. Doch dann stirbt wirklich einer der Mitwirkenden — und alle verdächtigen sich gegenseitig… 

Die niederländische Regisseurin Halina Reijn („Instinct“) hat den simplen Slasher-Plot als schwarzhumorig-paranoides Kammerspiel inszeniert. Statt grotesker Metzelszenen stehen die selbstverliebten Figuren im Fokus, die sich gegenseitig an die Gurgel springen. 

Ein weiterer Pluspunkt ist das wundervoll aufspielende Ensemble, das sich nie zu schade ist, sich der Lächerlichkeit preiszugeben. Zusammen mit messerscharfen Spitzen gegen die Oberflächlichkeit von Teilen der Social-Media-Generation bereitet das enormen Spaß.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: In Greater Manchester, upcycling expert Jacqui Joseph explores Altrincham recycling centre, hoping to discover unwanted items that can be revamped or revitalised and sold on for cash. Screen print artist Daniel Heath attempts to brew up a new look for a four-piece coffee table set, upholsterer Ollie Clueit has his hands full with a bulky three-seater sofa, while Jacqui gives a new lease of life to a pair of mid-20th-century deckchairs. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Push factors from the noisy, bustling cities of Britain, combined with the alluring peace of the countryside, has the population dreaming of homes in more scenic surroundings. Escape to the Country sees buyers from different areas on the UK considering their options to settle down in the English countryside. Presenters show off a range of prospective homes, before they must make their final decision towards the end of the show. Each episode taking place in a different region of the UK, we see a wide variety of beautiful homes across the country. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Mary Louise has made the journey down from Angus, bringing an oak lectern that has valuation expert Simon Bower beguiled. It's a 'proper' antique, which means Ian will always be interested, but exactly how does he plan to fit it in his caravan? The room goes international with our second item of the day, as Stephen comes all the way from Vienna to visit Leith Theatre. He's bringing a painting by celebrated Lancastrian artist James Isherwood, a name the dealers are sure to recognise. Fans of alliteration will enjoy debonair Duncan's dinky toys. Condition is king when it comes to these, though, so will he come to regret playing with them in his younger days? Next to face the dealers are sisters Liz and Sharon, selling some heavy gold masonic chains. Usually, scrap metal queen Mel would be the dealer to target, but with new dealers the Rag & Bone Bros in the room, she might face stiff competition. There's always space for an unusual musical interlude in the room, and today is no different. Jackie has brought along a Balinese gamelan, but will her exotic offering be enough to conjure up a bid from the dealers? (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Emma, Dave, Lee and Jodie – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: The Beasts
programme.desc: Ihr Engagement stößt jedoch auf heftigen Widerstand, vor allem bei den Brüdern Xan und Lorenzo Anta. Hintergrund ist ein Konflikt um den Verkauf von Land an eine Windkraftfirma: Während die Dorfbewohner auf Geld hoffen, blockieren Antoine und Olga das Vorhaben. Die Spannungen eskalieren durch Sabotage und gegenseitige Provokationen... \n\nInspiriert von realen Ereignissen. Hauptdarsteller Denis Ménochet kennt man aus der Einstiegsszene von „Inglourious Basterds“ (2009).

programme.title: Saving Lives at Sea
programme.desc: On the Northumberland coast, a 999 call comes in from a distressed woman whose husband is drifting out to sea on a paddleboard; the Seahouses crew race out to locate him. In Moelfre, north Wales, when a crew member at the station spots a kayak capsizing, the lifeboat launches to pluck the fishermen from the water. Out in the English Channel, a French vessel makes a distress call, alerting the Torbay crew. And in Calshot, Hampshire, a sailing sloop has become stuck on one of the area's notorious mudbanks – and is now taking on water. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: DIY SOS
programme.desc: In Southampton, the team comes to the aid of Ahmed and Rifat, a profoundly deaf couple whose dream home became a nightmare after a rogue builder abandoned the project. With three young children, no savings left and living on a building site, they need help to complete their home and make it work for their family's needs. Nick and the team call on the local community to transform both the house and the family's future. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Glorious Gardens From Above
programme.desc: Christine Walkden continues her airborne exploration of Britain's gardens by dropping in on the county of Essex. At the Beth Chatto Gardens, Christine experiments with triangular planting and shares tea and cake with a gardening legend. At RHS Hyde Hall, she shifts rocks with a former student, and it's all aboard a vintage Thames sailing barge for a trip on the Blackwater Estuary. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: How do you protect Britain's busiest mountain when more than 600,000 people visit each year? Charlotte Smith and Joe Crowley head to Yr Wyddfa, Wales's highest peak, to meet the people caring for its landscape and keeping visitors on the move. Joe joins volunteers tackling litter in some of the mountain's hardest-to-reach gullies before discovering work to protect rare alpine plants and the elusive Snowdon beetle, found nowhere else in the UK. Meanwhile, Charlotte goes behind the scenes at Wales's highest cafe to find out what it takes to keep visitors fed and watered at the summit. And Tom Heap investigates how organised crime gangs are targeting the countryside. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Landward
programme.desc: Dougie heads west to the Morvern Peninsula in Lochaber to find out how Ardtornish Estate is being run to balance farming and stalking with nature restoration. Anne is on a photoshoot in Glenshee with a portrait photographer using Scotland's landscape as her backdrop, and Leanna is near Kingussie encountering some misunderstood blood-sucking creatures that are being saved from extinction. Rosie visits the dairy farm near Peterhead that diversified and created new markets for their milk, and Dougie steps out with a herd of rare Irish cattle. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Best of Weatherman Walking: Northern Nostalgia.
programme.desc: Derek gets some northern nostalgia as he remembers three of his best walks in north Wales. Cadair Idris is a mountain steeped in legend and mythology – it's also one of Wales's most spectacular summits. Derek climbs to three peaks in this range and even braves an icy cold dip in its glacial lake, where the temperature, quite literally, takes his breath away. The second walk Derek recalls is from the Italianate village of Portmeirion, where he also discovers Y Gwyllt – "the wild" headland beyond. Finally, Derek walks the Dee Valley Way, a stunning 13-mile route which takes him from the pretty town of Corwen to its larger and more bustling neighbour, Llangollen. On the walk, he learns of a warrior prince and leads a horse-drawn barge along the Llangollen canal. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Saturday Kitchen Best Bites
programme.desc: Matt Tebbutt brings an abundance of autumnal flavours to the table with help from some Saturday Kitchen chefs. Bryn Williams celebrates the best of the season's produce with a delicious butternut squash and chestnut tart, served with a winter salad and crispy deep-fried sage leaves. Selin Kaizim brings a taste of Cyprus to the studio with her beef and bulgur wheat koftes, while David Carter makes aubergines the stars of the show. Julie Lin makes a dish packed with crispy fried fish, cucumber, melted cheese, a punchy sambal and a side of crinkle-cut fries. Poppy O'Toole adds spices and harissa to a classic cottage pie base before topping with a fresh chilli and herb mash. And Bryan Cranston and Marianne Jean-Baptiste battle it out for their food heaven. Meanwhile, Rick Stein sets out to prove that old-fashioned veg is best, and the Hairy Bikers learn the history behind one of the world's most famous condiments in Menorca. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Eva Longoria: Searching for France
programme.desc: Eva and her Breton guide Tanguy Thomassin explore the vast oyster beds of Cancale, oyster capital of Brittany. Being pummelled by one of the highest tides in Europe makes for fatter, sweeter and healthier oysters. And having once supplied King Louis XVI's oyster habit, Brittany still supplies half of France. Bretons also boast of plentiful sardines, kelp forests, spiny crabs and the rare cobalt blue lobster. Fished sustainably and cooked on a grill, it's little wonder that this beauty is called the king of lobsters. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Moose in the Glen
programme.desc: Multimillionaire landowner Paul Lister wants to turn his 23,000-acre estate north of Inverness into Europe's first wilderness reserve. Reinstating the old Caledonian pine forests is the first of his plans. He then wants to release long-lost animals, starting with moose and wild boar, and eventually predators such as brown bears, lynx and wolves. Some of the local people are far from convinced by Paul's vision. Will he even be allowed to let loose moose in the glen? (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: The team are in Gloucester, where presenter Paul Martin and experts Phillip Serrell and Michael Baggott discover some rare gems among the antiques and collectibles brought to the valuation day at the city's magnificent cathedral. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Celebrity Antiques Road Trip
programme.sub-title: Compilations, the Battle of the Pop Stars
programme.desc: From the road trip back catalogue, three of Tim Medhurst's favourite pop stars try their hand at our antiques-buying challenge. Vying to be top of the pops are 90s heartthrob Peter Andre, the golden boy of the new romantics, Spandau Ballet's Martin Kemp, and an 80s pop icon, the mega-glamorous Sinitta. They are guided along the way by experts Paul Laidlaw, Margie Cooper, and the "so macho" Tim Medhurst, helping them to hunt down timeless treasures. Sinitta lights up the saleroom with some illuminating items, Martin goes radio gaga, and Peter takes a punt on part of a plane! (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Wilderness with Simon Reeve
programme.desc: Simon Reeve travels across Mongolia – the most sparsely populated country on Earth and home to some of the most brutal and beautiful landscapes on the planet. Six times the size of the UK but with fewer than 3.5 million people, Simon wants to find out how nomadic traditions, such as hunting with golden eagles, and wild nature still shape everyday life, all while searching for the elusive snow leopard. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Eva Longoria: Searching for France
programme.desc: Sitting between Germany and France, Alsace is frontier land with a cuisine to match. In Strasbourg, Eva stops off at Brasserie Le Tigre for a beer (brassier means 'to brew') and a deliciously creamy tarte flambee. Then there's a trip to guide Coralie Andt's restaurant, known as a winstub, where French wines can be enjoyed with plenty of cheese and sausage – as well as more sausage with sauerkraut cooked in white Riesling wine. With French tarts in a brasserie that serves German-style beer, and German sausage in a winstub serving French white wine, Alsace is defined by its competing national influences. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: The Balkans: Europe's Forgotten Frontier.
programme.desc: Katya Adler travels to Romania, Kosovo and Serbia. In Romania, Katya visits what will soon be Nato's largest base in Europe. With Russia's increasing aggression, Nato's role in eastern Europe has been beefed up, and Romania has become strategically significant. Katya's next stop is Europe's youngest country, Kosovo. She travels down Tony Blair Street – named after the UK prime minister who led the Nato mission there. Twenty-five years after the war ended, Katya meets the ethnic Serbs who still live in Kosovo – and insist the country is still Serbian. Lastly, in Serbia, she visits a coal power plant and discovers there's a battle for power taking place, with the west, Russia and China all wanting Serbia to be in their sphere of influence. For decades, the west has ignored this corner of Europe, but now, with so many other parts of the world gaining power and influence, the fear is Europe might be losing its foothold in this increasingly important region. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: New: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing.
programme.desc: Paul and Bob travel to the River Ribble in Lancashire for one last fish with their little canine pal, Ted. The beautiful river Ribble runs through the rolling hills of the Yorkshire Dales, onwards to Lancashire before meeting the Irish Sea in Lytham. With the river in good health, Paul and Bob hope to catch a good chub or a mighty barbel on this stretch of the water, while Ted hopes to taste Bob's Lancashire hotpot. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: A Course Called Ireland *
programme.desc: Hollywood legend Bill Murray begins a journey around Ireland, combining golf with a search for his Irish roots. But travelling with Bill rarely goes to plan. In Kinsale, chance encounters turn a simple walk into an adventure, while friend and golf writer Tom Coyne tries to keep things on track. Golf brought Bill to Ireland, but the best moments often happen far from the course. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Later with Jools Holland
programme.desc: Jools welcomes, from Birmingham, Dexys Midnight Runners, who perform a couple of songs from their seventh album, LOVE, which was produced by David Holmes and offers a 'series of deeply personal scenes and reckonings'. Jools also chats to frontman Kevin Rowland, and the band share one of their classic hits from 1982. From Australia, singer-songwriter Courtney Barnett makes her debut on the show and performs two tracks from her album Creature of Habit, which "marks a decisive new chapter in her musical evolution" and was written in the wake of a relocation from Australia to Los Angeles. From Dublin, six-piece contemporary folk group Madra Salach appear ahead of their sold-out tour and perform their single Ribbon Factory, which is described by frontman Paul Banks as a 'uniquely Irish song and is wrought with anger and despair'. South London collective Ibibio Sound Machine also join the line-up to perform Concept of Love, taken from their album Chopping Mountain – 'a powerful album, promoting love, unity and resistance through music'. Born and raised in Bath, 19-year-old rising star Mulaa Joans makes her TV debut and performs the title track from her EP That Ain't You, described as 'an unapologetic anthem tackling modern dating fatigue'. Completing the line-up is the legendary singer-songwriter Elkie Brooks, known as the British queen of the blues, who this year celebrates 50 years in music. Jools chats to Elkie about the secret to her longevity, and together they perform the Bob Dylan classic Make You Feel My Love. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Film: Misery
programme.desc:
Nach einem Autounfall in den Bergen von Colorado wird der verletzte Autor Paul Sheldon (James Caan) von Annie Wilkes (Kathy Bates) aus seinem Wagen geborgen. Glück im Unglück: Die Einsiedlerin ist gelernte Krankenschwester und erweist sich als eingefleischter Fan von Pauls Romanen. 

Erst als sie sein neues Manuskript in die Finger bekommt, wendet sich das Blatt. Erbost über den geplanten Tod ihrer Lieblingsheldin Misery, verwandelt Annie das Krankenbett in eine Folterbank. Mit teuflischer Präzision zwingt sie Paul, den Schluss umzuschreiben…

Ein Jahr nach der Komödie „Harry und Sally“ bewies Rob Reiner, dass er sich auch meisterhaft auf Thriller versteht. Seine Adaption des Stephen-King-Romans „Sie“ hält den Zuschauer mit clever aufgebauter Spannung in Atem. Kathy Bates („Dolores“) erhielt für die Darstellung der gestörten Foltermagd den Oscar.

programme.title: Question Time
programme.desc: Is the UK already fighting in a proxy World War? Fiona Bruce presents topical debate from Scunthorpe, featuring defence secretary Wes Streeting for Labour, shadow foreign secretary Tom Tugendhat for the Conservatives, the Greens' Ellie Chowns, journalist and economist Stephanie Flanders and comedian and radio host Geoff Norcott. With defence spending expected to be increased in next week's Budget, watch what the Question Time panel from Scunthorpe said on hybrid "grey zone" warfare and threats from Russia, as well as new gas drilling in the North Sea, the state of the NHS and re-industrialising the UK. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Not Going Out
programme.desc: Lee is sceptical about all the witchy woo-woo stuff on display at an alternative craft fair where Lucy is trying to sell her badly made dream catchers. Unfortunately, his attitude irritates everyone there and ensures that Lucy can't sell any of her stock. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Ellie & Natasia
programme.desc: Ellie White and Natasia Demetriou make a chaotic return to the screen, reuniting with some of the show's most iconic creations – including a deeply passionate food review centred on bread, internet entrepreneurs Donna and Nikki trying to scale their beauty empire to dizzying new heights, and a duo of digital creators whose egos are only outsized by their wardrobe. Plus a guest appearance by Steve Coogan. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: While the teams get into the rhythm of their shopping, host Danny Sebastian indulges one of his passions at an exhibition in London. The Music Is Black: A British Story celebrates 125 years of the influence of black music on culture and communities. At the V&A East Museum, Danny tours the exhibition with curator Jacqueline Springer, looking at a vinyl record with the words "Race Records" on the sleeve, a label designed to segregate black music from white artists. There's a piano belonging to the first black artist to have a UK number one single, Winifred Attwell, engraved with the names of her fans, a dress worn by Dame Shirley Bassey at the 2013 Academy Awards and a Banksy-designed vest worn by Stormzy at Glastonbury in 2019. Hoping to turn their items into auction hits are dad and daughter Erike and Melissa, and mum and daughter Angela and Katie. With hundreds of stalls to choose from, the teams go in search of profitable antiques with their experts, Irita Marriott and Jonathan Pratt. While the red team sizes up a vintage measuring tape, the blues check out a crackle-glazed pig sculpture. Then it's off to auction in Bourne End, Buckinghamshire, to try to sell their buys to the highest bidders. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: The Great House Revival
programme.desc: Hugh meets designers Robin and Eoin on their journey to convert a Victorian schoolhouse into a chic family home. However, after delays and setbacks, can they transform this functional space into the home of their dreams? Presented by Hugh Wallace. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Match of the Day
programme.desc: A busy Premier League Sunday, with five matches, including Liverpool against a Brighton side who've started the season strongly, and Manchester United at home to struggling Bournemouth. Elsewhere, Brentford, another side who have enjoyed early-season form, travel to Hull City, two of last season's promoted clubs Sunderland and Leeds United meet at the Stadium of Light, and Pierre Sage's Crystal Palace take on Newcastle United. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc: Game show presented by Rick Edwards in which players score points by answering questions correctly. programme.title: Coast to Coast Food Festival
programme.desc: Edith Bowman and Colin Murray explore the Stranraer Oyster Festival, sailing into Loch Ryan to Scotland's largest wild oyster bed to discover why they're so special. Baker Briony-May Williams reveals the effort behind every bag of frozen peas, and farmer Meinir Howells goes underground to find the secret of cheesemaking in Harlech. Ryan Hand is in Armagh on the hunt for a healthy ready meal. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo embarks on a journey across Essex. Beginning on the fringes of London, he takes the underground to the ancient woodland of Epping Forest, with its gnarled hornbeams and beeches, a legacy of centuries of pollarding. Continuing on the Central Line, Michael visits a historic London Transport signal cabin in Epping which has been preserved by railway enthusiasts. He guides an underground train into Epping station – on a simulator. At Harlow, Michael visits the house and garden of the town's chief architect, Sir Frederick Gibberd. Michael hears about Gibberd's plan for Harlow's new town and discovers the architect's love of art and sculpture in the garden. At Audley End, he visits a charming miniature railway which has recently celebrated its 60th anniversary and learns of Audley End House's role as a secret wartime military school. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Madagascar: Earth's Tropical Islands.
programme.desc: Journey across the tropical island of Madagascar and explore the unique and incredible wildlife it has to offer – from its famed lemurs to chameleons. As the oldest island on earth, life has had time to evolve, and there are now more unique plants and animals on Madagascar than any other island. It was formed nearly 90 million years ago when a giant landmass split apart, and Madagascar was cast adrift from east Africa. Braving the 400-mile ocean crossing from Africa, the first castaways arrived on the arid west of the island, and were met with vast deserts. Ring-tailed lemurs are the direct descendants of one of the very first mammals to arrive, and they are thriving despite the arid conditions. They spend up to eight hours a day foraging in the Spiny Forest. Their plant-based diet includes plants with caustic sap that would burn human skin. When humans arrived on the west coast, they too faced the hostile desert, high temperatures and droughts that can last a year. In the village of Ampotaka, the people have learnt to use baobab trees to help them survive. The trees grow up to 30 metres high and store vast quantities of water in their trunks. By hollowing out the inside of the trunk, the people create huge water tanks storing thousands of litres of water, which they can use when times are tough. Tiny labord's chameleons are unique to Madagascar and have the shortest lifespan of any land vertebrate – living for just four months. They time their hatching with the start of the rainy season when the going is good, and then the race is on for them to grow, mate and lay eggs before the dry season comes round once again. One of the most dramatic places in Madagascar is known as the Grand Tsingy – 500 square miles of sharp limestone pinnacles sheltering small pockets of forest. To survive here, Decken's sifakas must climb these shards of rock, sharp enough to shred human skin, and leap 30 feet between them. A series of even higher peaks forms a mountainous spine running down the middle of Madagascar. Just a few thousand years ago, human settlers from Asia brought the skills to turn the steep mountainsides into rice paddies. By digging terraces into the slopes, even the steepest gradients can be farmed, producing more than a million tonnes of rice every year. But only if they can keep their crop safe from the devastating plagues of locusts in their billions. Madagascar's mountain range defines the islands' climate. It blocks warm, wet air blown in off the Indian Ocean to the east, creating the arid deserts of the west. But keeping all this moisture to the eastern side of the island makes rainfall high there, and this creates bountiful rainforests. Most of the island's incredible wildlife can be found within these tropical rainforests, including tenrecs, Madagascar's own unique version of a hedgehog. They give birth to more babies than any mammals – as many as 32 in a litter. The streaked tenrec rubs together modified spines on her back to make a squeaking noise to warn all her babies of danger. The extraordinary pelican spider twangs the threads of an orb web spider to lure it into its giant jaws. The aye-aye is one of Madagascar's weirdest creatures, found hunting for insect larvae at night. It uses it bizarre 9cm-long middle finger to tap tree branches for hollow bits, before scraping away the bark and deploying its super-sized finger to fish out the grubs. Madagascar's unique wildlife has slowly been evolving for millions of years, but since humans arrived, the pace of change has been faster than many animals can cope with. As little as 20 per cent of the island's original forest remains, and 95 per cent of lemurs are now threatened with extinction. The greater bamboo lemur is a story of how efforts to protect Madagascar's wildlife can save a species from being wiped out entirely. These lemurs were thought to have gone extinct, thanks to the clearance of the bamboo forests they rely on for food. The bamboo lemurs are now protected and in the last year, a record number of babies were born. Madagascar is at a critical point, but with the right efforts, there is some hope for its wildlife in the future. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Vintage Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel and the team visit Wilton House near Salisbury where a rich hoard of treasures and curiosities are brought to light. Included in the day's finds are a hoard of 200 typewriters, a suffragette doll dressed in clothes cut from women protestors' prison uniforms, a ring once worn by the daughter of Charles I, and an ornate table, transported in the back of a horsebox. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Flog It! comes to Blackburn in Lancashire, where the valuation day is being held at Blackburn Cathedral. The experts are Charles Hanson and Anita Manning. Anita discovers an Omar Ramsden spoon, and Charles finds an old silver bucket that has been used as a bin and a Christmas tree holder but turns out to be Faberge! Paul Martin learns about how mill workers in Blackburn during the industrial revolution were woken by a human alarm clock known as 'a knocker upper'. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Global Eye
programme.desc: A weekly programme from the BBC World Service, bringing forensic journalism from all corners of the world by BBC Eye, the World Service's critically acclaimed investigative unit, and featuring expert global correspondents getting to the heart of the biggest international stories. In this episode: Nawal Al-Maghafi reports from Yemen's front lines, where Houthi forces are posing the most serious threat in years to the city of Taiz, raising fears of a major escalation in a conflict that has endured for more than a decade. We also trace the roots of Yemen's war, exploring how the country's strategic location has drawn it into a struggle involving Saudi Arabia, Iran and the United States. Plus: BBC Mundo travels to Panama's Coiba Island, a biodiversity hotspot, to explore how a former prison colony helped preserve a rare and fragile natural world. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Escaping Idi Amin
programme.desc: In August 1972, Idi Amin is 18 months into his dictatorship. Supporters hail the new president – a former boxer and soldier – as a saviour, and his rise to power is greeted with celebration and hope across Uganda. But beneath the apparent social harmony, resentment runs deep. Until 1962, Uganda had been a protectorate of the British – with the British very much at the top of the pile, Africans at the bottom and Asians in the middle. Despite ten years of independence, many Africans feel that they are denied opportunities to improve their position in society. Idi Amin decides to exploit their feelings and increase support for his regime. With one announcement from the president, the lives of 80,000 people in Uganda are changed forever. In a bid to cement his leadership, Idi Amin announces that all Ugandan Asians must leave the country within 90 days. Will they be able to flee on their British passports? (Senderinfo).

programme.title: BBC Weather

programme.title: Shadowmen: Russians working with Ukraine.
programme.desc: Two Russian men secretly working for Ukraine's intelligence services give rare accounts of operations they claim to have been involved with, to target military assets and personnel inside Russia. One man, Ivan – not his real name – spent two years texting with and meeting Polish journalist Marcin Mamon. He describes himself as a Russian patriot but wants to bring down Putin's government. He says that helping Ukraine win the war could achieve that aim. Ivan shares the spycraft behind Ukrainian attacks on strategic bombers, and munitions factories, in Russia, and sends Mamon videos of his activities from inside the country. Over two years, Mamon establishes that Ivan is working for Ukraine – but can he be trusted? Mamon is taken into the shadow war between Ukrainian and Russian intelligence services, a world of agents and double agents, where the lines between being a patriot and traitor blur. Another operative Mamon meets is Foma, not his real name, exiled in Poland, who runs a network of volunteers in Russia who surveil high-level officers that the GUR – Ukraine's military intelligence service – is tracking. When a General is assassinated in December 2025, Foma confirms he was one of the individuals his team has tracked. The GUR confirm to Mamon that Ivan and Foma are working for them. It is impossible, however, to verify the activities they claim to have carried out because they have been cautious about how much detail they share. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: How do you protect Britain's busiest mountain when more than 600,000 people visit each year? Charlotte Smith and Joe Crowley head to Yr Wyddfa, Wales's highest peak, to meet the people caring for its landscape and keeping visitors on the move. Joe joins volunteers tackling litter in some of the mountain's hardest-to-reach gullies before discovering work to protect rare alpine plants and the elusive Snowdon beetle, found nowhere else in the UK. Meanwhile, Charlotte goes behind the scenes at Wales's highest cafe to find out what it takes to keep visitors fed and watered at the summit. And Tom Heap investigates how organised crime gangs are targeting the countryside. (Senderinfo).

And with lots of people now working from home, chef Julie Lin is on the hunt for healthy snacks. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael's exploration of Essex continues in Romford. He arrives on the London Overground's Liberty Line to visit a state-of-the-art rail operating centre, responsible for the whole of the East Anglian rail network. He discovers how signallers and operators control the movements of over 4,000 trains a day and learns how they respond to emergencies on the tracks. At Upminster, he finds the gateway to the Chafford Gorges nature park, which for centuries was exploited for its natural resources. The former chalk quarries have been transformed into a rare habitat for orchids, and he hears how archaeologists have discovered Neanderthal stone tools in the chalky cliffs. Michael takes a scenic rail journey through the marshy landscape of the Dengie Peninsula to arrive at a marina on the River Blackwater. He makes a choppy crossing to visit the Ross Revenge ship, home to Radio Caroline since the 1980s. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Borneo: Earth's Tropical Islands
programme.desc: In the heart of South East Asia, lies the tropical island of Borneo. Twice the size of the British Isles, it is the third largest island on earth and home to possibly the greatest diversity of life of any island. – from flying lizards sun bears to orang-utans. Its huge variety of habitats, from bustling coral reefs and ancient jungles to towering mountains, have given rise to over 60,000 species of plants and animals – many found nowhere else on Earth. Borneo's shoreline is fringed by a tangle of mangroves and flooded forests, home to an extraordinary creature – the proboscis monkey. Their unique pot-bellies allow them to survive on the nutrient-poor leaves, but even so, they must continually search for the freshest shoots. This means the whole family must cross one of many rivers that cut through the forest – patrolled by giant crocodiles. It's a drama rarely seen. The Island of Borneo is surrounded by some of the richest coral reefs in the world – a single reef can support more species of coral than the entire Caribbean Sea! This remarkable abundance attracted seafaring nomads, the Bajau Laut, 'People of the sea'. Over generations their bodies have transformed, making them the ultimate human divers – but they are having to adapt to the modern world – using ingenuity to turn plastic waste that washes up on the beach, to their advantage. Heading inland are ancient forests, home to giants – the Dipterocarps. Towering up to 100 meters high, they are the tallest rainforest trees in the world. A single tree can hold a thousand different species and this intense competition has driven many animals to evolve in wondrous ways – on this island reptiles can fly. At night, this competition in the jungle intensifies as many of Borneo's one hundred and eighty species of frog call for a mate. The bigger the frog, the louder the call: a problem for one of the smallest frogs on the island. In this never-before filmed sequence a male tree-hole frog, barely larger than a thumbnail, has come up with an ingenious solution to being heard above the noise. Compared to the abundance of life in the treetops, the forest floor is an impoverished world. With little to eat, many of Borneo's terrestrial mammals are smaller than on the mainland – including the exceedingly rare Bornean Sun Bear. At just over a meter long, it is the smallest bear in the world. To survive, they have developed a surprising skill – they are expert climbers, able to climb higher than any other bear, to feed on honey and fruits high up in the canopy. For those confined to the forest floor, more ingenious methods are required. The Penan are indigenous hunters that have lived in Borneo's forests for over 4000 years. They use a remarkable sign language, known as Oroo', to communicate through the jungle. A long stick is adorned with intricately folded vegetation and shaped bark, to tell a complex story. In the heart of the island, looming above the rainforest, lies another of Borneo's diverse habitats – mountains. Their range runs over 500 miles through the centre of the island. At over 4000 meters, Mount Kinabalu is one of the highest peaks in South East Asia. It rains here almost every day, the water washing away any goodness in the soil. To get the nutrients they need to survive, one group of plants have gone to extreme lengths. They've become carnivores. The modified leaves of pitcher plants form pitfall traps. Insects are lured to the traps' edge with sweet nectar, before slipping into a lethal pool of digestive enzymes. Borneo holds the greatest collection of pitcher plants in the world, including one that is after something much bigger than insects. Hemsleysana's is a pitcher plant that has evolved to attract woolly bats. Its traps are perfectly adapted to (Senderinfo).
